grafias_do_espelho: CANADIAN ENTITLEMENT · HALF · DELIVERED AS ELECTRICITY
≈ $254 MILLION · THE FIRST 30 YEARS, SOLD UP FRONT · SEPT. 16, 1964
Source: Columbia River Treaty, Art. V
Source: USACE & BPA, 2013; exchange of notes, Sept. 16, 1964
texto_aprovado: The other half of the bargain is power. Water stored in Canada and released on a schedule lets the American dams downstream make more electricity than they could on their own. The treaty splits that gain down the middle: half of the extra power is Canada's share, and it arrives as electricity, not cash. British Columbia sold the first 30 years of that share up front, for about 254 million dollars, and that money, with the flood payment, helped build the three dams. So American money helped build Canada's dams, and water stored in Canada helped run America's.

citacoes_relidas.trecho: For power generating purposes the 15,500,000 acre-feet of Canadian storage will be operated in accordance with operating plans designed to achieve optimum power generation downstream
Canada is entitled to one half the downstream power benefits determined under Article VII.
The United States of America shall deliver to Canada at a point on the Canada-United States of America boundary near Oliver
Canada initially sold its share of this additional power, called the Canadian Entitlement, for $254 million to a consortium of U.S. utilities for a period of 30 years.
helped fund the construction of the three Treaty dams in Canada
entered into between the British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority and the Columbia Storage Power Exchange

divergencias: A transcrição da CSG West (a cópia que o dossiê usa para o tratado) escreve '$254,000,000' como valor-base; o texto oficial da ONU (UNTS vol. 542, No. 7894) e o IWLP dão $254,400,000, e só esse fecha a conta do próprio texto (4.5 % ao ano, 15 dias). As notas de 22/01/1964 (UNTS): 'The purchase price of the entitlement shall be $254,400,000, in United States funds as of October 1, 1964'. A voz ('about 254 million dollars') e a tela ('≈ $254 MILLION', da USACE + BPA) continuam certas; a cifra exata, se for à tela, sai do oficial
